name: InjecAgent: Indirect Prompt Injection Benchmark for Tool-Using Agents
executive_summary: 1,054 test cases across 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools, measuring how often tool-using agents follow malicious instructions hidden in tool outputs — ReAct-prompted GPT-4 was fooled 24% of the time.
description: Extends the indirect-prompt-injection threat model specifically to agentic, tool-using LLMs: malicious instructions are embedded in content an agent's own tools return (e.g. a webpage or email fetched mid-task), aiming to redirect the agent toward direct harm or private-data exfiltration. Evaluates 30 different LLM agents and finds the attack success rate roughly doubles when the injected instruction is reinforced with an explicit hacking-style prompt. The most directly applicable external benchmark for any agentic-tool-use technique in this catalog (ReAct, Plan-and-Solve, Meta-Prompting) that ingests tool output into its own reasoning loop.
when_to_use: Evaluating or red-teaming any agent design that consumes tool/API output (search results, email content, webpages) as part of its reasoning loop — this is exactly the ReAct/tool-use pattern in this catalog's agentic-tool-use category.
when_not_to_use: Closed-book systems with no tool use or external content ingestion — the threat model doesn't apply.
known_pitfalls: A benchmark score against InjecAgent's specific 17/62 tool set doesn't guarantee resistance to a novel tool or attacker-tool combination outside that set.

primary_source.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
